note: Merged/ready real issue about routing every gh subprocess call through a shared helper; today's A4 autonomous_completion criterion false-positives on its own cross-cutting-sounding "every call" prose (known lexical-gate boundary gap).
title: fix(helpers): apply a default gh subprocess timeout and route every call through gh-exec
body:
## Background

`src/scripts/gh-exec.mts` is the shared `gh` execution layer, but it
does not apply a timeout by default and a large share of helpers do
not go through it at all. A stalled or credential-prompting `gh`
invocation therefore hangs the calling helper indefinitely, which in
an autonomous IDD session means a phase that never returns rather
than a phase that fails and routes to recovery.

Current state in `src/scripts/`:

- `ghApiJson()` calls `execFileSync('gh', args, { encoding: 'utf8' })`
  with no timeout and no option for a caller to supply one, even
  though it is the shared JSON entry point.
- `ghText()` applies a timeout only when the caller passes one; the
  default is no timeout.
- `GH_TEXT_LOOP_TIMEOUT_OPTIONS` (30s) already exists and is used at
  54 call sites, so a 30s bound is the established convention here —
  the gap is that it is opt-in.
- 30 call sites across 22 helper files still call
  `execFileSync('gh', ...)` directly, bypassing `gh-exec.mts`
  entirely; none of them pass a timeout.

Advisory review has flagged this shape repeatedly (for example, that
a per-run lookup loop calling `ghApiJson()` can hang the helper
because `gh-exec` sets no timeout), but each fix has been local to
the helper under review, so the underlying default has never changed.

## Proposed change

1. Give `gh-exec.mts` a default timeout. Apply a module-level default
   (the existing 30s convention) inside `ghText()` and `ghApiJson()`
   so a caller that passes nothing still gets a bounded invocation,
   and keep the explicit-option path as an override.
2. Let `ghApiJson()` accept a timeout override through its options
   object, so a caller that legitimately needs longer can ask for it.
3. Decide and record the paginated-call bound. `ghApiJson({ paginate:
   true })` can legitimately run longer than a single request, so
   either give the paginated path a larger default or document why the
   single-request bound is still correct. Record the choice in the
   module's doc comment so a later reader does not re-litigate it.
4. Migrate the 30 direct `execFileSync('gh', ...)` call sites in
   `src/scripts/**/*.mts` onto `ghText` / `safeGhText` / `ghApiJson`.
   Where a call site needs behavior `gh-exec` does not yet offer,
   extend `gh-exec` rather than keeping the direct spawn.
5. Add a guard test asserting that `gh-exec.mts` is the only module
   under `src/scripts/` that spawns `gh` directly, so the pattern
   cannot silently return.
6. Run `pnpm run build` so the generated `scripts/*.mjs` copies match
   their `.mts` sources.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ghText()` and `ghApiJson()` apply a bounded default timeout
      when the caller supplies none, and an explicit caller-supplied
      timeout still wins.
- [ ] `ghApiJson()` exposes a timeout override in its options type.
- [ ] The paginated-call timeout decision is implemented and recorded
      in `gh-exec.mts`'s doc comments.
- [ ] No module under `src/scripts/` other than `gh-exec.mts` calls
      `execFileSync`, `execFile`, or `spawnSync` with `'gh'` as the
      command.
- [ ] A guard test enforces the previous criterion and fails when a
      direct `gh` spawn is reintroduced into another module.
- [ ] Existing unit tests still pass, and helpers that previously
      passed `GH_TEXT_LOOP_TIMEOUT_OPTIONS` keep their 30s behavior.
- [ ] The generated `scripts/*.mjs` files are rebuilt and committed,
      and `node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check` reports no drift.
- [ ] The repository's `pre-push-validate` command passes.

---

below the configured floor is human-oriented._
